analysis:
Examined all supplied documentation excerpts, patches and file metadata against the canonical definition index and selected T-041 details. The visible changes introduce an add-on IPC reference/index entry and runtime-file documentation (docs/provider/cli-reference.md:1758); the surrounding benchmark, credential, attestation, fan-helper, logging and cache text is unchanged according to the complete range map. No concrete security regression is established by these documentation-only units.

The new docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md:12-25 specifies owner-only runtime files, conservative lock probing and a socket-path override. Lines 32-68 specify bounded framing/connections, lease limits, identifier-scoped operations, persisted active holds and lock-dependent expiry. Lines 72-97 claim per-request audit-token-based same-UID and signed/hardened-code verification, DEBUG-only alternate identity acceptance, and explicitly disclaim isolation from the shared OS user. This creates a serving-availability coordination contract relevant to ADV-001, TB-003, TB-007 and T-010/T-029, but does not itself demonstrate weaker prompt encryption, cache account isolation (T-041), serving authorization (T-053), billing or privileged fan authority.

Integration must validate these claims in ProviderCore/Addon/{AddonIPCServer,AddonPeerPolicy,AddonHoldPaths}.swift and the hold/admission lifecycle: fresh code identity after exec, release versus a still-held ownership lock, restart recovery, bounded handler/connection cleanup, and safe resumption without bypassing serving authorization or retaining inference resources. The CLI mailbox behavior at changed lines 904-932 is not supplied in full here. The new reference cites TB-012 at line 97, which is absent from the BASE canonical index; reconcile the PR's threat-model update with this new coordination surface. Missing implementation is a coverage limit, not evidence of missing controls.
